page: Amazon Web Services c8a.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the platform exposes 96 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core, reaching clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The system includes 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per core compute-focused ratio. It features 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core complex, complemented by modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and bfloat16. There are no discrete GPUs and no bundled local storage devices, requiring attached network storage over its 40 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results place the server in the top tier for raw computational density and throughput. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves top-decile metrics for both single-core (3,776.89) and multi-core (349,774.63) operations. This performance carries over to Geekbench with a single-core score of 2,591.0 and a multi-core score of 30,249.0, alongside strong software compilation throughput of 88,178.0 in Clang. Memory subsystems deliver high-bandwidth throughput, recording 518.29 GB/sec in large-block read operations. Extended vector extensions allow the server to deliver strong CPU-based machine learning prompt processing, exceeding 6,660 tokens/sec on small language models.

The bare-metal deployment eliminates hypervisor overhead and virtualization jitter, providing deterministic latency for parallel processing. The primary hardware tradeoff lies in its storage architecture: the absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network volumes, which may constrain IOPS-intensive pipelines unless mitigated by network-level caching. The 1:2 core-to-memory distribution also limits utility for workloads with large per-thread memory footprints, favoring high-concurrency computation over in-memory capacity.

The hardware configuration is suited for compute-intensive batch processing, video encoding, continuous integration software compilation, scientific simulations, CPU-based machine learning inference, and static web serving environments requiring steady multi-core execution.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.metal-24xl is a compute-optimized bare-metal server driven by a 96-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. With dedicated single-threaded physical cores, the platform provides 96 vCPUs, 192.0 GB of memory, and a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no integrated local storage or discrete graphics accelerators, routing storage traffic through external network interfaces. Synthetic and application benchmarks highlight top-tier multi-core computing power, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 30,249.0, strong Clang compilation throughput, and high-bandwidth cached memory reads exceeding 16,842 GB/sec. Hardware support for AVX-512 and bfloat16 delivers efficient CPU-based inference and cryptographic operations. The system is suited for CPU-heavy tasks such as distributed software builds, parallel simulations, high-volume web serving, and compute-bound batch analytics.
